en:
All right, then, I guess I'll tell the third story.
My name's Makoto Shindo.
Class 3-D.
You know our school's a big name in sports, right?
Well, with this many students, of course we're strong.
And it's not just sports, either.
It's not like we've got a lot of smart kids or anything, but the sheer numbers are on a whole other level from your average high school.
That's why a bunch of our guys end up getting into Tokyo University.
Me, I'm not much for studying, so let's leave that side of things alone.
Let me talk about sports instead.{p}

Sports are great.
There's only one championship.
It's not like college entrance exams, where it's just a choice between passing or failing.
There's only one top spot.
And you fight each other for it.
Plus, you don't hear about many people who study because they love it, right?
But sports are different.
It's nothing but people who love it, pitting their strength against each other.
And they all aim for that one and only top spot.
Now that's what youth is about, huh?
So, {a}.
Don't spend all your time studying.
Turn your eyes to sports a little, and burn up your youth on something besides studying.{p}Maybe you don't need me telling you that, though. Do you play any sports?
I do
I don't
I'm planning to start soon

...Anyway, that's enough of that.
It's fine to burn with obsession for a sport.
But don't get so into it that what you're burning with turns from obsession into a grudge.
You know how when a person dies holding a grudge, they become an earthbound spirit, right?
When that happens, they say the spirit picks the place it was most attached to.
Most of the time, people who die full of resentment and grudges are the ones who got murdered or killed themselves.
So they end up becoming earthbound spirits right where they died.
Especially spirits that got killed with a whole lot left undone in this world. They say those can't let go of their attachment to life, and they can't leave that spot.{p}

People who play sports have a strong drive to win, right?
And the harder they work, the stronger it gets.
So imagine one of them suddenly dying in an accident.
And imagine it happened just a few days before a big tournament.
They couldn't rest in peace even in death, right?
So they become an earthbound spirit.
And not where they died, either. They become an earthbound spirit in the place where they practiced their hearts out.
You don't hear many stories about someone who studied themselves into a nervous breakdown and died, then showed up as a ghost in a classroom, right?
That's not because they loved studying more than anything. It's the opposite: they hated it more than anything.
So there's no way they'd become earthbound spirits.
The gym and the athletic field are different, though.
There's a good chance the people who died still hung up on their sport turn into earthbound spirits.
Ever heard about the crack of a bat from fielding practice on an empty field?{p}
Arai's story touched on this earlier, too.

Stories about hearing a basketball bouncing in the gym in the dead of night, or shouts and cheering and footsteps echoing there... you must've heard one at least once, right?
Those are all earthbound spirits who couldn't forget the sport they loved, coming back as ghosts.{p}

Well, it's a sad story, isn't it?
They had something they could throw themselves into, and their short lives came to an end after little more than ten years.
But listen, don't go feeling sorry for them.
If you sympathize, the spirit will take advantage of you.
What I'm about to tell you is the story of a guy who went through hell just because he felt sorry for a spirit.
The captain of the basketball club is in my class.
And our basketball club has a certain legend.
Basketball's a popular sport these days, sure.
But about ten years ago, even getting enough members together was a struggle.{p}

Back then, a guy named Yoshiki Tadokoro was the captain.
That year, too, they couldn't find any good new recruits, and he was racking his brains over how to make the team stronger.
Tadokoro wanted to make it to the national tournament somehow, and he was desperate.
That's when a much-hyped new recruit joined the track club.{p}

The new kid's name was Kawaguchi.
In junior high, Kawaguchi was a sprinter who got a fair bit of attention.
What caught Tadokoro's eye was Kawaguchi's height.
A full 185 centimeters.
Pretty impressive, right?
Kawaguchi had a sprinter's explosive speed and, with some pretty solid marks in the long jump, great leaping ability too.
Exactly the kind of talent you'd want to make a team stronger.{p}

So Tadokoro tried to land Kawaguchi no matter what it took.
But the track club wasn't going to just sit back and let that happen, right?
Kawaguchi was the track club's great hope for an ace in the first place.
Having the basketball club steal their star would be a raw deal.
Even when they warned him, Tadokoro's recruiting just kept escalating.{p}

Finally fed up, the third-years in the track club called Tadokoro out and beat him up. It was practically a lynching.
But that Tadokoro guy had some real guts.{p}What do you think he did?
Told a teacher about it
Told Kawaguchi what the track club was really like
Photographed his own beating and blackmailed the track club with it

That's right.
Tadokoro had somebody take pictures of him getting beaten, then turned the tables and used them to blackmail the track club.{p}

Even the track club guys had to throw in the towel on that one.
They stopped laying a hand on Tadokoro after that.{p}

But the real problem was how Kawaguchi felt.
No matter how hard he recruited, if Kawaguchi had no interest in playing basketball, it was pointless.{p}So how do you think Kawaguchi actually felt?
Didn't want to quit track
Wanted to join basketball
Actually didn't really want to do sports
Kawaguchi had been doing track ever since junior high.{p}

On top of that, Kawaguchi had set a string of records, and had the results and the confidence to show for it.
What reason would there be to quit?
No way Kawaguchi would want to quit.
That's also why the track club guys decided to just leave Tadokoro alone.{p}

Even so, Tadokoro clung on for dear life.
He stuck to Kawaguchi's side and wouldn't leave, almost like a lover.{p}

Eventually, even the basketball club guys got fed up with Tadokoro's methods.
Then, one or two at a time, members started quitting the club.
Maybe they never liked basketball all that much to begin with.
Tadokoro didn't miss guys like that, either.
His head was already full of nothing but Kawaguchi.
It was like he thought landing Kawaguchi alone would clinch the championship.
Still, that's not realistic, right?
And then, little by little, rumors about Tadokoro started reaching the teachers' ears.
I mean, members really were quitting one after another, and the captain never showed up to practice because he was off chasing after Kawaguchi.
And finally, Tadokoro got kicked out as captain.
Which was only natural, but Tadokoro couldn't understand it.
He was pouring so much passion into basketball, so why didn't anybody understand that? He just couldn't figure it out.
Well, I guess that's what you call twisted passion.
Guys like that are seriously scary when you make 'em mad.{p}What do you think he did?
Went to complain to a teacher
Harassed the new captain
Decided to quit the basketball club

Believe it or not, Tadokoro quit the basketball club.
He loved basketball, loved it more than anything.{p}

But the school's basketball club didn't just fail to understand that, it even got in his way.
He figured they were jealous of his talent, or else it was harassment from the other, talentless members.
Honestly, selfish people are selfish all the way down.
They only ever see things the way that suits them.
The guy was practically a psycho.
So he decided that sticking with basketball alongside such twisted people wasn't good for him.
Honestly, who's the twisted one here?{p}

So in the end, he decided to quit the club.
Nobody objected.
If anything, they were glad.
The guy getting in the way would be gone, they figured.
Both sides thought the other one was in the way, so I guess in a way everybody was happy.
It all worked out in the end, after all.{p}

So he went to clear his stuff out of the club room.
And not just his own locker, either. He tore through the whole room.
He figured if there was anything useful, he'd just help himself to it.
What a total lowlife, huh?
So, like it was spring cleaning, he turned over everything from the desks to the lockers, rummaging around for this and that.
It was less like cleaning and more like he was rampaging through the club room, trashing the place.
And when he dragged one of the lockers out, he found a single grimy notebook in the gap behind it.{p}

The spot for the name was stained, so he couldn't make out whose it was.
When he opened it, it was full of all kinds of stuff about the basketball club from back in the day.
Some senior from generations back must've written down what happened in the club, like keeping a diary.
At first he was just idly flipping through it, but little by little, he got drawn into what it said.{p}So what do you think was written in it?
Gripes and complaints about the basketball club
Something about Tadokoro
How to summon a demon
An incident that caused trouble years ago

At first, it was all about how much the writer loved basketball.
Passion for basketball, plus all kinds of research on effective practice methods and even diet.{p}

Tadokoro was moved by it.
By the fact that there'd once been a senior in this very club room who loved basketball more than anything, just like he did.
But as he kept reading, wouldn't you know it, things started going in a strange direction.
It turned into gripes and complaints: the people around him didn't understand his love for basketball, the other members didn't share his commitment, that kind of thing.
And then that turned into bitter words cursing the members and the teachers, and helpless rage.
It was exactly how Tadokoro felt right now.
"There was a senior who felt the same way I do..."
Tadokoro lost all track of time, absorbed in that notebook.
And the notebook ended with the writer saying he would kill himself in the gym and take revenge on everyone.
And then...{p}

'P.S. To a kindred spirit who feels as I did.
If you should ever read this notebook, I want to help you.
At two in the morning, in the gym, call out that you want help.'
That's what it said.
You can't imagine how shocked Tadokoro was.{p}

And at the same time, he was trembling with joy.
He wanted to meet the person who wrote this notebook so badly he couldn't stand it.
And if he could meet him, his problems were sure to be solved.
He didn't doubt it for a second.
Tadokoro was completely convinced that the notebook existed just for him.
The notebook was Tadokoro's now.
So he went to the gym.{p}

Well, of course he did.
But can you believe it?
The guy he wanted to meet was dead.
And a total stranger, to boot.
Sneaking into school in the middle of the night just to meet somebody like that? I sure wouldn't want to.
Then again, maybe only a psycho like Tadokoro would.
At exactly two in the morning, Tadokoro went to the gym.
And under the basketball backboard, he shouted.{p}

"I need help!
You, the senior who felt the same way I do!
Please, help me!"{p}...What do you think happened?
The senior's ghost appeared
He heard only a voice
It's too frightening for me to even imagine

...No voice answered.
I mean, that notebook was fishy to begin with.
It could've been somebody's prank.
That's what anybody would normally think, right?
But Tadokoro didn't give up.
And he shouted again.
"Please! I'm begging you!
Help me!
I want to meet you!"
He was grasping at straws.
Tadokoro wished from the bottom of his heart to meet him.{p}

And then, guess what?
"...I'm so happy.
To think someone would call me this soon..."
A voice actually answered!
But there was no one to be seen.
Tadokoro looked all around.
Maybe it was because it was dark, but he couldn't see a thing.
Tadokoro reached for the switch to turn on the lights.
"Don't turn them on!"
That's what the voice said.
Maybe it didn't want to be seen.
Thinking that, Tadokoro pulled his hand back.
There was still no one to be seen.
Even so, Tadokoro was happy.
After all, he'd met a person who felt the same way he did.
...Oops, not a person. A ghost.
After that, the two of them talked for a while in the gym in the dead of night.
About how much each of them loved basketball, and why other people couldn't understand that.{p}

"I understand how you feel...
I understand it so well it hurts.
I know exactly what you're going through."
The bodiless voice sympathized with Tadokoro.
And it told him how bitter it had felt, too.
"I understand, I really do.
It must have been so frustrating.
If I'd been there back then, I definitely could have helped you.
When I think that I couldn't help you, I'm so sad I can't stand it."
The two of them talked until dawn.
And as the sun was coming up, the voice said:
"...Now, go on home for today.
I have to go back too.
If you'd like, come anytime.
There's only so much I can do, but I want to help you, little by little."
"Thank you so much!"
And then the voice was gone.{p}
And then night came again.{p}What do you think Tadokoro did?
Went to the gym again that night too
For no particular reason, didn't go that night
Something happened to come up that night, so he couldn't go

No way he wouldn't go.
No matter what came up, Tadokoro would've gone.
He could hardly wait for two in the morning.
After that, for a while, their secret late-night meetings went on almost every day.{p}

Here he had someone who understood him, and yet he couldn't do anything.
Then he remembered what was written in that notebook.
The senior had said he would help.
If so, Tadokoro wanted that help right now.{p}

So that night, Tadokoro asked the voice.
He asked it to help him.
"I see.
...There's only so much I can do.
But you're just like me, aren't you?
I suppose I could help you.
...Yes, you're worth helping."
"Really?!"
Tadokoro jumped for joy.
"...Yes, really.
But if I'm going to help you, I'll have to show myself.
I'm going to appear in front of you now, so would you keep your eyes closed until I say it's okay?"
"Okay. I will."{p}

Tadokoro closed his eyes.
It was pitch-dark either way.
He couldn't see a thing.
But, you know, you can still feel a presence.
He could feel it with his whole body: something had appeared right in front of him.
You could call it a chill, I guess.
That feeling where your whole body starts shaking even though it isn't cold.
Something had definitely appeared in front of him.
"...All right, you can look now."
The voice came right by his ear.
Not the faint voice from before, the one he couldn't tell where it was coming from, but a voice clearly whispering right in his ear.{p}So, should he open his eyes?
Open his eyes
Keep them shut a bit longer

Tadokoro swallowed hard.
And then he opened his eyes all at once.{p}
"Aaaaaghh!"{p}

What stood before him was himself, rotted all the way through.
Himself, so changed he looked like a corpse that had crawled out of its grave.
You know what a doppelganger is?
It's your other self.
They say if you meet it, you'll die before long.{p}

...The next day, Tadokoro was found dead in the gym.
They say his face was frozen in terror, too hideous to look at twice.
In the end, it was put down to Tadokoro losing his mind and killing himself in the gym.
The cause of death is unknown.
Officially, they're calling it a heart attack.{p}

...That's the story they pass down in the basketball club.
How does anyone know it, if Tadokoro died, you ask?
Hm hm hm... What do you think happened to that notebook?
I hear it's still somewhere in the basketball club.
Though they say it's not easy to find, even if you go looking.
And what's more, there's a second volume.
Of course, as for who wrote the second one... you know, don't you?
And what was written in it, too.
The story goes that someone found it by chance and read it.
That's why this story keeps getting passed down.
You do sports, right?
I don't know what you play, but don't overdo it.{p}
...By the way, do you have an older brother?
Yes
No

Ask whether he's got some secret he's hiding.
And then, if your brother goes pale...
Hm hm hm, you'd better watch yourself too.
That's the end of my story.
Let's hear the next one.{p}

If you're thinking about starting a sport at this school... there's something I want to warn you about.
At our school, people who play sports have had all kinds of encounters with spirits.
There's a lot of dangerous stuff going on.
Sports are about pushing yourself to your limits, right?
It's an all-out, serious contest.
So the passion of people who play sports is something else.{p}

Did you know?
When a person's will is strong, spirits are more likely to go after them.
There are spirits that slip into the cracks in your heart, like wanting to get stronger or wanting to beat somebody, and do their dirty work.
To avoid that, you need a heart strong enough to throw spirits off.
{a}, you'd better build up a heart like that too.
It'd be stupid to stay out of the sports clubs just because spirit stuff happens more there.{p}

Still, no matter how strong your heart is, there are plenty of ways to fall into a trap.
So on top of a strong heart, you need to keep your eyes open too...
Let me tell you about a certain athlete.
The boys' volleyball team at our school went away to summer training camp.
The camp lodge is one of our school's facilities.{p}

It's a building that came with some land the school bought, and they just use it as is.
It's up in the mountains, and apparently it used to be a school.
It's wooden, a shabby old building that looks like it could fall apart any minute.
But since it was a school, it's got a gym.
So the clubs use it a lot for training camps.{p}

...If you join a sports club, you might end up going there for camp too.
The roof leaks and the walls are covered in stains. It's seriously creepy.
And you lay out futons and sleep right there.
Maybe it's the perfect place for some sweat-and-guts sports drama.
But I hear things show up a lot when you go there for camp.
What shows up?
Spirits, obviously.
Everyone says you hear a woman crying, or moaning, or that there's a human-shaped stain on the wall.
So, about that boys' volleyball camp.
...{p}

The camp ended without a hitch.
But when they got back to school, there was one more ball than before.
The first-year who was sorting the club's equipment noticed something was off.
But he thought it might just be his imagination, so he didn't tell anyone.
That's when it all started.{p}

Players started getting hurt, one after another, during practice.
At first it was just scrapes from falling, or twisted ankles.
But as time went on, there were accidents like torn Achilles tendons and broken bones.
That went on for about a month, and everyone started to think something was strange.
So the team members thought it over.
The injuries on the boys' volleyball team had started... right around when they... got back from camp.
Then one day, there was a practice match against another school.
They invited the volleyball team from a nearby high school to play at our school...{p}

After that, a first-year on the team started saying the ball was what was suspicious.
When they got back from camp, there'd been one extra ball.
Everyone scratched their heads, wondering if there had even been any balls at the camp lodge.
But if it was true, they decided they'd better do something about that ball.
Everyone figured that if it had come from that lodge, it made perfect sense for it to be cursed.
But the club had about twenty balls in storage.
There was no way to tell which one was the extra.
Still, they couldn't afford any more accidents.
So, just to be safe, they threw out every ball the boys' volleyball team had at the time.
Then they went and bought twenty brand-new balls.
And after that, the accidents at practice stopped dead.
Strange things happen, huh?
Everyone kept telling each other what a scary business that had been.
But then...
One day, about two weeks later, there was one extra ball in the club's stock again.
This time, they could tell exactly which one it was.{p}
Because among the newly bought balls, there was one single ball that was old and filthy.{p}That's right, the cursed ball had come back...
Have it exorcised
Throw the ball out again

They couldn't let there be any more victims.
That's what everyone thought, so they decided to have an exorcism done.
One of the members saw an ad tucked in the corner of a magazine and brought in an exorcist.
And the exorcist started saying something like this:
"This ball is possessed by the spirit of a student who died in an accident.
It seems he was on a volleyball team, and was hit by a car on his way to an important match.
It's better to perform the exorcism at night.
I'll come back here tonight, and I'd like one of you to come along with me then..."
So a first-year on the team ended up going with the exorcist.{p}

He was the one who'd first noticed there was an extra ball after camp.
His name was... Matsumoto, I think.
Matsumoto was the great hope of the boys' volleyball team.
He'd been playing volleyball since elementary school.
His father was a P.E. teacher, and apparently taught him all kinds of things.
He was tall, and his jumping ability was outstanding.
Plus, in junior high, he'd been on the team that won the Tokyo tournament.
Matsumoto had a good personality, too.
Nobody would want to go along to an exorcism at school at night, right?
But when it came up, he was the first to volunteer.
And so Matsumoto arranged to meet the exorcist at the school that night.{p}

It was a chilly day, right as autumn was setting in.
Matsumoto showed up about twenty minutes before the agreed time.
But the exorcist was already standing at the school gate.
"I've been waiting for you..."
The exorcist said that with a smile.
Seeing it, Matsumoto shuddered.
It should have been nothing but a polite smile, but he couldn't help finding the exorcist creepy.
He only felt that way because the school was scary at night.
That's what Matsumoto told himself.
The exorcism was to be held in the gym.{p}

The two of them crossed the schoolyard, one step at a time.
Heading for the gym, Matsumoto felt a chill creeping up his spine, colder and colder.
There wasn't any wind, yet it felt like something was passing across his back.
It felt like something cold was licking at him from behind. Swish... swish...
And then, when the two of them entered the gym...{p}

A ball was lying all alone on the floor.
It was that cursed ball.
At noon that day, they were sure they'd put the ball away in the gym storeroom.
So why was it here now...?

Matsumoto started shaking violently.
But he couldn't very well go home now.
"Well then, Matsumoto.
Let's begin the exorcism."
The exorcist was grinning.
Why was the exorcist grinning?
What was this person grinning about...?
"Matsumoto... I'm so happy.
To think you'd help someone like me.
Now, pick up the ball over there.
And hold it tight against your chest."{p}

Matsumoto did as the exorcist said.
Or rather, it felt like his body moved on its own.
Something was wrong with this exorcist.
Even thinking that, he couldn't resist.
"Now, pray while you hold the ball.
For the spirit of the athlete who never got his due.
Save him, with your pure heart that loves sports..."
Matsumoto prayed with all his might.
If he'd been killed in a car accident before a match, he might not be able to rest in peace either.
Matsumoto could feel that athlete's bitterness as clearly as if it were his own.{p}

"Ah... Matsumoto.
I'm so happy... thank you.
Thank you... You understand how I feel, don't you..."
Before long, the exorcist started saying things like that.
"More... pray more...
Then I can rest in peace... and the ball's curse will be lifted.
If I, if only I can rest in peace..."
The exorcist's form changed into a boy in a gym uniform, blurred in a faint white haze.
Matsumoto kept praying desperately.
"Thank you. Thank you.
Thank you..."
The boy in the gym uniform faded into the haze and vanished...
At the same moment, the ball in Matsumoto's hands vanished too.{p}

All that was left was Matsumoto, alone in the gym at night...
Do you get what that means?
The spirit of the athlete who'd cursed the ball had shown up disguised as the exorcist.
And he'd gotten Matsumoto to pray his soul to rest.
Apparently the real exorcist who'd taken the job got into a car accident and never made it.
The whole thing had been set up by the athlete's spirit.{p}

...Whoa, the story doesn't end there.
It's about Matsumoto.
The moment the athlete's spirit passed on, Matsumoto felt a violent pain in his legs and arms.
But there was no calling for help in the gym at night, and they say he writhed all alone on the cold floor.
Matsumoto couldn't stand.
The pain in his legs and arms was so bad he couldn't even crawl.
Before long, his eyes started to hurt too.
And then Matsumoto passed out...
The next day, Matsumoto was found collapsed.
The bones in his legs and arms were broken.
His ankles had been twisted, and his Achilles tendons were torn.
He was covered in bruises and wounds, and the surface of his eyes was scratched...
That's right. It was everything that had happened to the people the ball's curse had hurt.
All of it hit Matsumoto at once.
And the people hurt by the ball's curse all made a full recovery.
As the price for lifting the ball's curse, Matsumoto ended up sacrificing his own body...{p}

How about that, {a}?
Sports are great.
But if you go to this school, you've got to stay careful even during club practice.
Don't go sticking your nose into anything reckless.
Though I'd say this seven wonders interview of yours is already pretty death-defying.
That's as far as my story goes.
Want to hear the next one...?{p}

The ball rolled by itself across the schoolyard, all the way to the volleyball club room.
The club room door was shut at the time.
But the ball slipped right through the door and got inside.
Then it set the club room on fire, starting a small blaze.
The members scrambled to put it out.
Luckily, the fire went out quickly.
But...{p}

Black soot and scorch marks were left caked onto the charred club room wall.
And those scorch marks...
Were in the shape of a person.
They say the shape looked just like the stain on the wall at the camp lodge.
What shape do you think it was?{p}
...That's right, it was shaped like an athlete holding a ball.

Long ago, when that camp lodge was still a school, a volleyball player apparently died in an accident.
That spirit must have seen our school's camp and envied them.
It turned itself into a ball and followed everyone back.
It hurt everyone because it wanted them to notice it was there.{p}

And they did notice, all right.
But instead of laying the spirit to rest, they threw it into the incinerator...
Well, I'd say the spirit went about it the wrong way too.
In the end, that spirit held a grudge over how the team treated it and became an earthbound spirit.
Apparently that club still gets a lot of injuries even now.
...{p}

Listen, {a}.
A strong heart and a watchful eye. That's what matters.
If you're going to start a sport, that is...
That's as far as my story goes.
Who's telling the next one...?{p}

I see...
Everyone who doesn't play sports gives that answer.
Like they're scrambling to cover it up.
Nobody's saying it's bad not to play sports.
Well, whatever.{p}

That's right.
Tadokoro got someone to take photos of him being beaten, and went to show them to a teacher.{p}

That's exactly it.
Tadokoro got someone to take photos of him being beaten, and went to show them to Kawaguchi.{p}

And he tried to talk Kawaguchi into quitting the track team and coming over to basketball.
But Kawaguchi figured the track seniors must have had some reason for doing this.
After all, the track seniors had always been kind to Kawaguchi.
The way Kawaguchi saw it, they'd done what was in those photos to protect Kawaguchi from Tadokoro's clutches.
So this is what Kawaguchi told Tadokoro:
Kawaguchi wouldn't be joining basketball.
But Tadokoro didn't give up.
After that, he kept coming around to see Kawaguchi, still pushing for the basketball team.{p}

You think so?
Kawaguchi had been doing track ever since junior high.{p}

Well, it seems that was true at first.
Kawaguchi's old man used to hold a sprint record back in the day.
Kawaguchi got into track because of the old man.
Kawaguchi did it grudgingly at first, it seems, but the kid had talent.
After setting record after record, Kawaguchi started taking sprinting seriously, the story goes.
So no matter how hard Tadokoro recruited, Kawaguchi's mind didn't change.{p}

Tadokoro talked to the team members.
He asked them to make him captain again.
But everyone kept their mouths shut and said nothing.
Tadokoro was so frustrated he couldn't stand it.
He loved basketball, loved it more than he could bear.{p}

Hey, {a}.
You know the word 'sportsmanship,' right?
You always hear it at the opening ceremonies of school sports days and track meets.
"We, the athletes, pledge to compete fair and square in the spirit of sportsmanship..."
